annotation.summary_en: In a parody of a Los Angeles support group, two newcomers—a sophisticated artist and a blunt Armenian immigrant—share their progress on addiction and imagination.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: Set in a bare cream-walled room in Los Angeles (dated December 24, 2004), five men sit in a circle on office swivel chairs for a group therapy session. The therapist leads the group in a collective relaxation exercise before opening the floor. Two regulars share their progress about overcoming past relationships and alcoholism, with a character named Bob constantly repeating exactly what the previous speaker said to the therapist's approval. The session introduces two newcomers: Juan, a sophisticated man from Mexico, and Hendo, a blunt immigrant from Armenia. Juan delivers a poetic testimony about how six months of studying art and literature helped him quit drinking, while Hendo admits he has only been drug-free for two hours since arriving in America. For a final 'imagination' test, the therapist has them look out the window. Juan describes a complex vision involving Rembrandt, Michelangelo's David, and Zeus. When it is Hendo's turn, he humorously admits he was going to say he saw a little elephant and a fish but changed his mind after hearing Juan's high-brow response.
catchphrases: ես ուզում էի ասեի որ տեսնում եմ փղիկ ու ձկնիկ
